Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 307 of 2004
With
Jail Petition No. 02 of 2005
lawyer:
Abdul Baset Mazumder; Senior Advocate, with J.B.M. Hassan instructed by A.S.M. Khalequzzaman, Advocate-on-Record. ------ For the Petitioner.

Paritosh Rudra -----Petitioner.

full_judgment:
Md. Hassan Ameen J: This petition for leave to appeal as well as Jail Appeal Preferred by condemned-prisoner, Paritosh Rudra, is directed against the judgment and order dated 18-07-2004 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Jail Appeal No. 615 of 2002 heard with Death Reference No. 50 of 2002 dismissing the appeal and accepting the Reference and thereby affirming the judgment and order dated 28-10-2002 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Cox's Bazar in Sessions Trial Case No. 81 of 2001 convicting him (petitioner) under Section 302 of the Penal Code and sentencing him to death. 

 2. The prosecution case, in brief, is that one Purnendu Bikash Rudra of Kakara, Cox's Bazar on 04-12-2000 filed a petitioner of complaint before the cognizance Court No.2, Cox's Bazar, alleging, inter-alia, that about four and half years before the date of occurrence his (complainant) daughter, Sunita Rudra was married with the accused Paritosh Rudra and they were blessed with a daughter namely Nishi Rudra and that in the event of failure of the informant to give dowry, the Paritosh Rudra had been torturing Sunita both physical and mental. The accused was residing with his wife and daughter in a rented house of one Nur Mohammad of Nheela Puratan Bazar, Teknaf. On 09-11-2000 at about 4.30 P.M. the informant received a message at Chakoria that his daughter and grand daughter (Sunita and Nishita respectively) were murdered in their residence, the complainant rushed there immediately and found the dead bodies. In the aforesaid facts and circumstances, the informant suspected that the accused Paritosh murdered his daughter and grand daughter with the help of miscreants and in order to save himself, the accused earlier lodged an FIR with Teknaf Police Station which is pending as G.R. No. 208 of 2000 and thereafter, the informant also filed G.D. entry on 13-11-2000 with the said Police Station bringing allegations against Paritosh. The said petition of complaint having been referred to Teknaf Police Station was recorded as Teknaf Police Station Case No.20 dated 25-12-2000 under Sections 302/34 of the Penal Code against the accused-petitioner, Paritosh. 

 6. The defence case as could be gathered from trend of cross-examination of prosecution witnesses is total denial and his case, inter-alia, is that he is not responsible for, nor connected with the murder but has been falsely implicated in the case out of grudge and enmity. 

 7. The trial court in consideration of the evidence on record as well as facts and circumstances of the case found the accused guilty of the offence charged and as such convicted him thereunder and sentenced him to death. 

 9. Mr. Abdul Baset Mazumder, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the learned Judges of the High Court Division misconceived the law as well as facts of the case and thus without proper assessment of materials on record confirmed the sentence and as such the impugned order is liable to be interfered with, for ends of justice. He further submits that the evidence on record was not properly sifted and thereby caused miscarriage of justice. 

 10. Learned Advocate lastly submits that the alleged sole eyewitness Anwar Hossain (Pw.3) was examined long after 2 months of the occurrence and as such his evidence ought to have been left out of consideration and in view of the facts and circumstances of the case, he submits that there is good ground for critical examination of the materials on record and as such prayed for leave to appeal. 

 12. The learned Judges of the High Court Division affirmed the conviction and sentence so passed by the trial Court after proper appreciation of evidence on record and the learned Advocate for the petitioner failed to dislodge the same by any cogent argument. In such facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the opinion that there is no substance in this petition for leave to appeal and accordingly, the petition for leave to appeal is dismissed.
